points.title: 童年与艺术启蒙
points.description: 安迪·沃霍尔出生于宾夕法尼亚州匹兹堡的斯洛伐克移民家庭。幼年时期，他患有风湿热，导致长期卧床，这期间他开始绘画和收集电影明星照片。沃霍尔在卡内基理工学院（现卡内基梅隆大学）学习商业艺术，这段经历培养了他对商业与艺术结合的兴趣。他的早期作品已展现出对流行文化和名人肖像的关注，为后来的波普艺术风格奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Andy Warhol was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania to Slovak immigrant parents. As a child, he suffered from rheumatic fever, which kept him bedridden for extended periods. During this time, he began drawing and collecting photographs of movie stars. Warhol studied commercial art at the Carnegie Institute of Technology (now Carnegie Mellon University), where he developed an interest in the intersection of commerce and art. His early works already showed an interest in pop culture and celebrity portraiture, laying the foundation for his later pop art style.

points.title: 商业艺术家转型
points.description: 沃霍尔移居纽约后，成为一名成功的商业艺术家，为《时尚》、《魅力》等杂志工作，同时为知名品牌如可口可乐、宝洁设计广告。他逐渐在艺术界崭露头角，1952年首次举办个人展览。这一时期，沃霍尔开始探索丝网印刷技术，并创作了《金宝汤罐头》和《可口可乐瓶》等标志性作品，这些作品将日常消费品转化为艺术，挑战了传统艺术与商业的界限，标志着他从商业艺术家向波普艺术大师的转变。
points.descriptionEn: After moving to New York, Warhol became a successful commercial artist, working for magazines like Vogue and Harper's Bazaar, and designing advertisements for major brands such as Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble. He gradually gained recognition in the art world, holding his first solo exhibition in 1952. During this period, Warhol began experimenting with silk-screening techniques and created iconic works like 'Campbell's Soup Cans' and 'Coca-Cola Bottles,' transforming everyday consumer products into art and challenging the boundaries between traditional art and commerce, marking his transition from commercial artist to pop art master.

points.title: 波普艺术巅峰
points.description: 这一时期是沃霍尔艺术生涯的巅峰阶段。他在纽约东村建立了'工厂'工作室，那里成为艺术家、名人、地下电影人和社交名流的聚集地。沃霍尔创作了《玛丽莲·梦露》系列、《电椅》系列和《灾难》系列等标志性作品，将名人、死亡和暴力等主题融入艺术。他还开始涉足电影制作，创作了《睡眠》和《帝国大厦》等实验性电影。1964年，他的作品在纽约现代艺术博物馆展出，获得国际声誉。沃霍尔通过艺术探索消费主义、名人文化和大众媒体的关系，成为波普艺术的代表人物。
points.descriptionEn: This period marked the peak of Warhol's artistic career. He established his 'Factory' studio in New York's East Village, which became a gathering place for artists, celebrities, underground filmmakers, and socialites. Warhol created iconic series such as 'Marilyn Monroe,' 'Electric Chairs,' and 'Disasters,' incorporating themes of celebrity, death, and violence into his art. He also began experimenting with filmmaking, creating experimental works like 'Sleep' and 'Empire.' In 1964, his work was exhibited at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, earning him international recognition. Warhol explored the relationship between consumerism, celebrity culture, and mass media through his art, becoming a leading figure in the pop art movement.

points.title: 遇刺与转型
points.description: 1968年，沃霍尔在其工作室'工厂'被女权主义者瓦莱丽·索拉纳斯枪击，险些丧命。这一事件导致他重新审视生活和艺术，风格变得更加内省和多样化。他开始创作更多肖像画，包括米克·贾格尔、毛泽东和伊丽莎白·泰勒等名人。沃霍尔还创办了《访谈》杂志，将艺术、时尚和名人文化融为一体。这一时期，他的作品更加注重色彩和形式实验，同时保持了对流行文化的关注。尽管经历了生命危险，沃霍尔的艺术创作反而更加活跃，成为20世纪最具影响力的艺术家之一。
points.descriptionEn: In 1968, Warhol was shot by feminist Valerie Solanas in his 'Factory' studio and nearly died. This incident caused him to re-examine his life and art, leading to a more introspective and diverse style. He began creating more portraits, including those of Mick Jagger, Mao Zedong, and Elizabeth Taylor. Warhol also founded the magazine 'Interview,' blending art, fashion, and celebrity culture. During this period, his work focused more on color and formal experimentation while maintaining his interest in pop culture. Despite the life-threatening experience, Warhol's artistic activity became even more prolific, establishing him as one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 沃霍尔晚年继续创作，并开始探索宗教主题，创作了《最后的晚餐》系列。他与年轻艺术家如让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特合作，影响了一代新人。1987年，沃霍尔在纽约接受胆囊手术后去世，享年58岁。他的葬礼吸引了众多艺术界和名人界人士参加。沃霍尔去世后，他的作品价值飙升，成为世界上最昂贵的艺术品之一。他创立的安迪·沃霍尔博物馆在匹兹堡开放，成为美国专门献给一位艺术家的最大博物馆。沃霍尔的艺术遗产持续影响着当代艺术、时尚和流行文化，他本人已成为美国文化的标志性人物。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Warhol continued to create and began exploring religious themes, producing the 'Last Supper' series. He collaborated with younger artists like Jean-Michel Basquiat, influencing a new generation. In 1987, Warhol died in New York following gallbladder surgery at the age of 58. His funeral was attended by numerous figures from the art and celebrity worlds. After his death, the value of his work skyrocketed, making some of his pieces among the most expensive in the world. The Andy Warhol Museum opened in Pittsburgh, becoming the largest museum in the United States dedicated to a single artist. Warhol's artistic legacy continues to influence contemporary art, fashion, and pop culture, and he has become an iconic figure in American culture.

appraisal.zh: 沃霍尔被普遍视为20世纪最具革命性的艺术家之一，他打破高雅艺术与大众文化的界限，把日常消费品与名人肖像提升为艺术主题，借“工厂”培育新一代创作者，预见了艺术与商业、媒体融合的趋势，其影响延伸至观念艺术、街头艺术与数字艺术，名字几乎成为波普艺术的同义词。另一种看法认为，他的作品过于商业化、缺乏深度与原创性，丝网印刷简化了创作过程，对消费主义不加批判甚至加以美化，后期创作重复早期模式而失去探索的勇气。
appraisal.en: Warhol is generally seen as one of the most revolutionary artists of the 20th century: he broke the boundary between high art and popular culture, raised consumer goods and celebrity portraits to artistic subjects, nurtured a new generation through the Factory, and anticipated the fusion of art with commerce and media, his influence reaching conceptual, street and digital art, his name nearly synonymous with pop art. Another view holds that his work was overly commercial and lacking in depth or originality, that silk-screening simplified the creative process, that he was uncritical or even celebratory toward consumerism, and that his later output repeated earlier formulas without the courage to explore.

supporter.zh: 沃霍尔被誉为20世纪最具革命性的艺术家之一，他打破了高雅艺术与大众文化之间的界限，将日常消费品和名人肖像提升为艺术主题。他的波普艺术不仅挑战了传统艺术观念，还反映了消费主义社会的本质。沃霍尔通过'工厂'工作室创造了独特的艺术社区，培养了新一代艺术家。他的作品具有前瞻性，预见了当代艺术与商业、媒体融合的趋势，对后来的观念艺术、街头艺术和数字艺术产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Warhol is hailed as one of the most revolutionary artists of the 20th century who broke down the barriers between high art and popular culture, elevating everyday consumer products and celebrity portraits to artistic subjects. His pop art not only challenged traditional artistic concepts but also reflected the essence of consumerist society. Through his 'Factory' studio, Warhol created a unique artistic community and nurtured a new generation of artists. His work was visionary, anticipating the fusion of contemporary art with commerce and media, and has had a profound influence on later conceptual art, street art, and digital art.

critic.zh: 批评者认为沃霍尔的艺术过于商业化，缺乏深度和原创性，只是简单复制流行图像。他被指责为艺术界的投机者，利用名人效应和市场营销手段获取名利。沃霍尔的丝网印刷技术被一些评论家视为简化了艺术创作过程，降低了艺术的技术门槛。此外，他被批评为对消费主义持不加批判的态度，甚至美化消费文化。沃霍尔后期作品的重复性和缺乏创新也成为批评焦点，有人认为他后期只是在重复早期的成功模式，失去了艺术探索的勇气。
critic.en: Critics argue that Warhol's art was overly commercial, lacking depth and originality, merely replicating popular images. He has been accused of being an opportunist in the art world, leveraging celebrity status and marketing tactics for fame and fortune. Warhol's silk-screening technique has been criticized by some as simplifying the artistic process and lowering technical barriers to art. Additionally, he was criticized for his uncritical attitude toward consumerism, even glorifying consumer culture. The repetitiveness and perceived lack of innovation in Warhol's later work also became points of criticism, with some arguing he merely repeated his early successful formulas, losing the courage for artistic exploration.

objective.zh: 从历史和流行文化视角看，沃霍尔已成为美国现代文化的标志性人物，他的名字几乎与波普艺术同义。沃霍尔的艺术反映了20世纪后半叶美国社会的变迁，特别是消费主义、媒体文化和名人现象的兴起。他成功地将艺术与商业、时尚和媒体融合，预见了当代艺术的发展方向。沃霍尔的影响超越了艺术领域，延伸到时尚、音乐、电影和商业设计等多个方面。他的'15分钟名人'概念已成为流行文化中的常用语，反映了现代社会对名人和媒体的关注。沃霍尔的艺术遗产持续影响着当代艺术家的创作方式，以及公众对艺术与商业关系的理解。
objective.en: From a historical and pop culture perspective, Warhol has become an iconic figure in American modern culture, his name almost synonymous with pop art. Warhol's art reflects the social changes in the latter half of the 20th century America, particularly the rise of consumerism, media culture, and celebrity phenomena. He successfully merged art with commerce, fashion, and media, anticipating the direction of contemporary art development. Warhol's influence extends beyond the art world into fashion, music, film, and commercial design. His concept of '15 minutes of fame' has become a common phrase in popular culture, reflecting modern society's fascination with celebrities and media. Warhol's artistic legacy continues to influence how contemporary artists create and how the public understands the relationship between art and commerce.

self.zh: 在未来的某个时候，每个人都能成名15分钟。
self.en: In the future, everyone will be world famous for 15 minutes.
